newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish prime minister names new key ministers.
newsitem.headline: Polish prime minister names new key ministers.

text.p: Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz chose liberal Wieslaw Kaczmarek on Thursday to head Poland's new ministry of the economy.
Cabinet chief-of-staff Leszek Miller has been tapped as minister of the interior and administration, Cimoszewicz told PAP news agency.
The two ministries are to be created on New Year's Day under a cabinet shake-up agreed within the leftist coalition government in October.
Kaczmarek, a former privatisation minister, is currently deputy treasury minister. His new ministry will be in charge of industrial and foreign trade policies.
The October agreement allocated both of new jobs to members of the Democratic Left Alliance, the larger of the coalition partners.
Its junior partner, the Polish Peasant Party, is to get the treasury portfolio.
Cimoszewicz told PAP he had sent the nominations to President Aleksander Kwasniewski who was likely to announce the appointments on Friday.
The cabinet reorganisation, due last for several more months, provides for several new ministries, merging some and liquidating others.
Cimoszewicz said he had not yet proposed a candidate for the labour minister, a portfolio vacant since Andrzej Baczkowski died last month.
